question.text: Satpura Market-Neutral Fund (a Cat III AIF) is computing its tax withholding on derivatives income before passing returns to investors. Per Section 2.6.1, which statement correctly characterises the tax position of an India-based Cat III AIF relative to offshore hedge funds?

answer.text: Cat III income is fully tax-exempt; offshore hedge funds face higher tax
Cat III income is taxed via PASS-THROUGH to investors under Section 115UB, with 10% TDS under Section 194LBB

Cat III income is taxed AT THE FUND LEVEL, requiring the fund to withhold 42.7% of all derivatives income before distributing to investors — giving offshore hedge funds a comparative tax advantage in several jurisdictions
Cat III is taxed like a listed equity mutual fund at 10% LTCG flat

explanation.text: The Logic: Section 2.6.1 states: 'The income of Category III AIFs are taxed at fund level, requiring the fund to withhold 42.7 per cent of all income on derivatives trading before they pass on the returns to investors.' Offshore jurisdictions often provide more favourable treatment, which is why offshore hedge funds enjoy a tax-advantage comparator. Cat III is specifically EXCLUDED from the Cat I/II pass-through regime. The Trap: Option A is fictitious. Option B is the CAT I/II pass-through treatment (Section 115UB + 194LBB) — a classic Cat I/II vs Cat III swap trap. Option D is MF-style tax applied to AIF incorrectly. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-D (Cat I/II Manager) tests 115UB pass-through + 194LBB TDS — that is THEIR tax regime. XIX-E here tests the OPPOSITE: Cat III is fund-level MMR (approx. 42.744% for derivatives income at AOP rates). XIX-C (All-Cat) contrasts the two. Manager's Pro-Tip: The 42.7% fund-level tax-drag is why Cat III managers increasingly evaluate a GIFT-IFSC domicile under Section 80LA for a 100% tax holiday on specified income for 10 consecutive years out of 15. The tax-drag haircut at fund level is arithmetic — it directly reduces the post-tax TWR your LPs see, so build the tax saving into your Sharpe/Sortino benchmarking, not just gross P&L.
